{{short description|Dutch–Australian geophysicist}}
[[File:Kurt Lambeck headshot.png|thumb|Portrait photograph of Kurt Lambeck for the 2018 Prime Minister's Prize For Science.]]
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2019}}
Professor '''Kurt Lambeck''' [[Order of Australia|AC]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science|FAA]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New South Wales|FRSN]] (born 20 September 1941 in [[Utrecht]], [[Netherlands]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.balzan.org/en/prizewinners/kurt-lambeck/bio-bibliography_1971_1975.html |title=International Balzan Prize Foundation |accessdate=2013-03-07 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130414120730/http://www.balzan.org/en/prizewinners/kurt-lambeck/bio-bibliography_1971_1975.html |archivedate=2013-04-14 }}</ref>) is Professor of [[Geophysics]] at the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra, Australia]]. He has also taught at [[University of Paris]] and at Smithsonian and Harvard Observatories.<ref>[http://people.rses.anu.edu.au/lambeck_k/index.php?p=bio Biography]{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, Research School of Earth Sciences, anu.edu.au</ref>

His current research interests include the interactions between ice sheets, oceans and the [[solid Earth]], as well as changes in ocean levels and their impact on human populations.<ref name=science>[http://www.science.org.au/media/pres2006.htm Earth Scientist Elected New President of Science Academy] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081121025452/http://www.science.org.au/media/pres2006.htm |date=2008-11-21 }}, www.science.org.au</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Lambeck was President of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] from 2006 to 2010. He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of London]] and the [[Royal Society of New South Wales]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Fellows of RSNSW |url=http://royalsoc.org.au/society/fellows.htm |publisher=RSNSW |accessdate=25 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320074313/http://royalsoc.org.au/society/fellows.htm |archivedate=20 March 2012 }}</ref> as well as the recipient of many prestigious international awards.<ref name=science/> He is a member of the French Academy of Science, the US National Academy of Sciences, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, Academia Europaea, and the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40120|title=Gruppe 3: Geofag|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=Norwegian|accessdate=7 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927170926/http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40120|archive-date=27 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> Lambeck is a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 1993.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4433 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160208204548/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/4433 |title=K. Lambeck |publisher=[[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |date= |archive-date=8 February 2016 |accessdate=8 February 2016}}</ref>

*2012 Awarded a prestigious [[Balzan Prize]] for his work on Solid Earth Sciences, with emphasis on interdisciplinary research.
*2013 Made a Chevalier de la [[Légion d'honneur]] by the [[Cabinet of France|Government of France]] for his work at [[CNES|Centre national d'études spatiales]] in the 1970s.<ref>{{cite news|title=Canberra scientist awarded highest French decoration|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-03-06/canberra-scientist-awarded-highest-french-decoration/4557028|publisher=ABC|date=6 March 2013}}</ref> 
*2013 Awarded the highest award granted by the [[Geological Society of London]], the [[Wollaston Medal]] recognizing lifetime achievements and service.
*2015 Awarded the [[Matthew Flinders Medal and Lecture]] by the [[Australian Academy of Science]]<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.science.org.au/node/40388#.VfvnFn2Exdw|title= Australian geologist receives top national honour|publisher= [[Australian Academy of Science]]|accessdate= 18 September 2015|archive-date= 15 August 2014|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140815143152/http://www.science.org.au/node/40388#.VfvnFn2Exdw|url-status= dead}}</ref>
*2018 Awarded the [[Prime Minister's Prizes for Science|Prime Minister's Prize for Science]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/science/2018-10-17/2018-prime-ministers-prize-for-science/10384228|title=Geophysicist who helped make GPS accurate gets top PM Science Prize|last=Osborne|first=Tegan|date=2018-10-17|work=ABC News|access-date=2018-10-17|language=en-AU}}</ref>
*2021 Appointed [[Order of Australia|Companion of the Order of Australia]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emeritus Professor Kurt Lambeck AO|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/2009384|access-date=2021-06-13|website=It's An Honour}}</ref>
